# NimoteCode Full Context

> NimoteCode is a mobile IDE and project development workspace for Android, iPhone and iPad. Open local files or connect to a development host over SSH to edit code, run project commands and review changes. AI is optional.

## Product capabilities and boundaries
- Local workspaces support file browsing and editing. Opening a local folder does not provide a Linux shell, compiler or project runtime.
- SSH workspaces use the connected host’s projects, tools and account permissions.
- Local Linux provides root-free Ubuntu on supported Android 8+ ARM64 / x86_64 devices. It is not available on iPhone or iPad; project tools and dependencies must be installed separately.
- Git review includes status, diffs and history. GitHub integration supports repositories, issues, pull requests, reviews and CI workflows subject to account permissions.
- Nimote Agent can read project files, plan changes and run checks. Confirm mode requires plan approval. Users can follow execution steps, add instructions during a run and review the resulting changes.
- AI Chat and the built-in Agent require the user’s own provider and API key (BYOK). NimoteCode does not include model credits; provider usage is billed separately.
- Compatible external ACP Agents require separate runtime setup and credentials. Claude Code and Codex can be used through SSH when installed and authenticated on the host; they are not bundled tools.
- Free features include local and SSH workspaces, editing, basic terminals and Git review. Agent, Git write operations, GitHub integration, Local Linux, LSP, debugging and plugins are Early Access features. Check the current entitlement page and app for availability.
- Language services and debugging require compatible tools in the target environment. Custom plugins and saved tasks extend project workflows.

## Notes
- The public site separates conversion-focused marketing, guides and product updates from task-oriented documentation under `/docs/`.
- The public documentation is intentionally concise so LLMs can use the linked pages as focused context rather than scraping the entire site.
